source_uses.fact: Planning should ensure development is suitable for ground conditions and address landslide, subsidence, ground heave and mining-related instability where relevant
Most development in a mapped Development High Risk Area requires a Coal Mining Risk Assessment, subject to exemptions
Planning advice service for Development High Risk Areas was updated 25 June 2026 and is intended to address coal-mining legacy risks through design and implementation
Current advice states the developer remains responsible for ensuring development is safe and stable
Current official tools expose coalfield planning and development information, historic mining plans and mine-water data
Official WMS layers include coal mining reporting areas, mine entries, planning policy constraints and specific risk
NPPF ground-conditions policy requires adequate site-investigation information and places responsibility for safe development on developer/landowner
Planning should ensure land is suitable for its new use and contamination is considered alongside other regulatory regimes
EA introduced a site-specific voluntary remediation advice service on 3 June 2026 for contamination affecting controlled waters
Draft London Plan 2026 includes geodiversity within GHR6 and remains draft policy
Draft London Plan site-capacity policy is strategic and does not replace ground investigation or geotechnical design
The 2026 Integrated Impact Assessment work incorporates environmental evidence and mitigation considerations at strategic-plan scale

examples: A national coal-risk dataset does not mean a Barking and Dagenham parcel lies in a coalfield or High Risk Area
A Development High Risk Area match would trigger assessment requirements but not automatically make development impossible
A low-risk coal map result cannot exclude unrecorded hazards without using current official location data
Land-stability guidance requires competent assessment where ground conditions warrant it
Contamination and instability are separate risk pathways even when both concern the ground
EA voluntary remediation advice is site-specific regulatory advice and is not a generic parcel value signal
Draft geodiversity policy is strategic context and not a geotechnical result
No promotion without exact parcel coordinate/polygon relation and appropriate current ground-risk evidence
